Ha-NhaP was determined to be a K+/H+ antiporter and shown to confer strong K+ resistance both at acidic and alkaline stresses.

1.q: a ΔHa-nhaD2 mutant exhibited growth inhibition at high Na+(Li+) concentrations at pH values of 6.2, 8.0, and 10.0, suggesting its physiological role in osmotic homeostasis.

2.q: Ha-Mrp showed central roles in the pH homeostasis of Halomonas sp. Y2. An Ha-mrp-disrupted mutant was seriously inhibited by high concentrations of Na+(Li+, K+) but only under alkaline conditions.

3.q: deletion of ke1 markedly decreased the egress of K+ and thus resulted in obviously reduced growth in medium containing 1.6 M KCl and various concentrations of NaCl

4.q: high transcript levels of Ha-mrp in response to the stress of 1.6 M K+ ions at pH 10.0 correlate with the impaired K+ extrusion ability and growth of the mrp-deficient strain... the Mrp system in strain Y2 is critical to K+ resistance under high alkalinity

5.q: Two NhaD-type antiporters, NhaD1 and NhaD2, from the halotolerant and alkaliphilic Halomonas sp. strain Y2, exhibit different physiological functions in regard to Na+ and Li+ resistance, although they share high sequence identity.
